title: Widest Spacing for M Markers
statement:
A straight road has free spots at the distinct positions in spots (not sorted). You must place m markers, each on a different spot.

The spacing of a placement is the smallest distance between any two of its markers. Return the largest spacing you can achieve.

examples.why: Markers at 1, 4 and 9 have gaps 3 and 5. Asking for a gap of 4 everywhere only fits two markers (1 and 6).
Two markers go on the only two spots; the input order does not matter.
1, 5, 8, 12 has gaps 4, 3, 4. A gap of 4 everywhere fits only 1, 5 and 12.

hints: Turn the question around: for a fixed gap d, can you place all m markers so that every two neighbours are at least d apart?
With the spots sorted, that check is greedy: put a marker on the first spot, then on the first spot at least d further, and so on. Starting as early as possible never hurts.
If gap d is achievable, every smaller gap is too. So binary search the largest d that passes the greedy check.

explain.intuition:
Finding the best placement directly is hard, but checking a proposed gap is easy. Sort the spots and walk left to right, dropping a marker whenever you are at least d past the last one. Placing each marker as far left as possible leaves the most room for the rest, so if this greedy walk cannot fit m markers, nothing can.

The check is monotone: a gap that works keeps working when you shrink it. That is the shape binary search needs. Search the gap between 1 and max − min, keeping the largest one that passes.
steps: Write fits(d): place the first marker on spots[0], then place one on each spot at least d past the previous marker. Return whether you placed m.
Binary search d in [1, spots[n−1] − spots[0]]: if fits(mid), the answer is at least mid; otherwise it is below.
pitfalls: Forgetting to sort. The check only works when you walk the road from left to right.
Taking a midpoint that rounds down in a 'find the largest' search, with lo = mid. It loops forever when hi = lo + 1; round up or keep a separate answer variable.
Searching over spot indexes instead of distances. The answer is a distance, and it may not equal any single difference you would guess first.

complexity.time: O(n log n + n log R), R = spread of the spots

solutions.title: Try every pairwise distance
solutions.idea: The answer is always the distance between some two spots. Try those distances from largest to smallest and return the first that the greedy check accepts.

solutions.title: Binary search on the gap
solutions.idea: Sort once, then binary search the largest gap for which the greedy left-to-right placement fits all m markers.
solutions.time: O(n log n + n log R)

followups: Return the positions of one best placement, not just the spacing.
The spots arrive one at a time and you must answer after each one. What would you keep between queries?
